source.title: Codex Cloud run status (Game lanes without their own Issue)
source.body:
Status board for Codex Cloud tasks of Game lanes that have no Issue of their own (mechanics and package lanes).

Each Cloud task writes ONE comment here, whose first line is `run_id=<id> state=READY|PROGRESS|BLOCKED|DONE|FAILED stage=<step> [sha=<40 hex>]`, and keeps editing that same comment. The coordinator's monitor reads these comments by `run_id`. Do not discuss tasks here; the comments are machine status only.

Lanes that have their own Issue report there instead.

This is built on the publicly available Claude Code SDK.

Reviewed PR #3304 at `729b3b3caec0f4a574a0ec8a6828d85b86ba1f73` against `0370259b379155bed91abe3873d568ce12d4bd6c`. Game preflight returned READY at the requested head.

1. **P1 — Cargo directives fail the required architecture check.** `crates/gameplay/dispatch/build_pg_shards.rs:8` (also lines 9, 10, 14, 26, 28 and 32). The merge gate's “Verify machine workspace boundaries” command counts these seven new `println!` sites as console output. I ran the command at this head and it failed with `direct console output rose for crates/gameplay/dispatch: 9 > 2`. Account for Cargo build-script directives in the checker or its reviewed baseline.
2. **P1 — The fixture split breaks the duplicate-test-source gate.** `apps/game-server/tests/support/character_revision_sequencer_postgres_cases.rs:1009`. Both the default dispatch library harness and the game-server `durability_postgres` integration target include the new six-test file. The guard's exemption names the old file, which now has no test attributes. Running its comparison with those two source lists reports `character_revision_sequencer_pg_tests.rs defines tests compiled into 2 test targets` and leaves the old exemption stale. Preserve the intended two-target exception at the new path or separate the test owners.
3. **P1 — Three moved sealed implementations fail the integration inventory.** Under `crates/gameplay/dispatch/src/gameplay_transport/postgres_tests/support/`, the affected sites are `bed_sleep_fixture.rs:31`, `kill_reward_e2e/summer_handoff.rs:6` and `qn1_elemental_world_pin/handoff.rs:21`. I ran the game-server seal inventory. It reported all three new paths as unapproved and all three previous paths as stale. Move the corresponding entries in `apps/game-server/tests/sealed_impl_allowlist.txt` with their implementations.
4. **P1 — Two dispatch unit tests still pin the old room-gate locations.** Examples are `crates/gameplay/dispatch/src/gameplay_transport/postgres_tests/support/m25_ahau_exit_fixtures.rs:115` for a room construction and `support/all_charms_secondary_fixtures.rs:308` for an accessor call. Both inventories key on the exact source path. Running the 14 tests from `bundle_gates_tests.rs` in isolation against this checkout reproduced exactly two failures, `a_bundle_world_seam_has_no_qualified_room` and `every_gate_call_is_inventoried`. Reconcile both maps with the relocated sites, retaining the per-file counts.
5. **P1 — Fixture path edits invalidate five reward qualification records.** Under `crates/gameplay/dispatch/src/gameplay_transport/postgres_tests/`, see `qready1_reward_claims.rs:122`, `qready2_claims.rs:5` and `qready2_purple_claims.rs:3`. The completion-matrix loader hashes those files and raises `Reward USE test changed; rerun PostgreSQL` at this head. I checked every stored digest: qready1, qready2 batches 1–3 and qready2-purple all match the base and all fail on the head. Preserve the pinned source bytes or renew the evidence through its qualification process.
6. **P1 — The shard checker omits 70 real tests from its inventory.** `tools/repository/check_dispatch_pg_shards.py:20` accepts only literal function names. The current mounts generate 28 tests with `damage_cases!` in `all_charms_outgoing.rs:64`, 28 with `quest_case!` in `source_quest_rewards.rs:82` and 14 with `native_case!` in `srvenc_source_deaths.rs:24`. The checker reports 2,250. Its scan of `source_quest_rewards.rs` returns zero tests both before and after dropping `thais_lighthouse_rewards` in a temporary copy. Compare actual Rust-discovered names or cover the expansions. The macro invocations themselves match the base.
7. **P1 — CI executes neither the shard check nor its three regression tests.** `tools/repository/test_check_dispatch_pg_shards.py:9`. The governance loop invokes each file as `python "$test"`. This file defines a TestCase and exits successfully without calling `unittest.main()`. Explicit discovery ran all three. No workflow invokes `check_dispatch_pg_shards.py 3`, and the unit tests never call its full `check(3)`. A broken partition or exceeded source budget can pass this gate.
8. **P2 — A common omission in the default and shard builds passes the checker.** `tools/repository/check_dispatch_pg_shards.py:108` derives the expected names entirely from the head's generated mounts and explicitly adds them to the scan independently of the Rust owner's generated-file include. Deleting a literal test from all builds, marking it ignored, or dropping the owner's `include!(concat!(...))` can therefore leave the union check green. Compare with an independent baseline and retain ignored status when checking preservation.
9. **P2 — Incremental Cargo builds can reuse an obsolete assignment.** `crates/gameplay/dispatch/build_pg_shards.rs:32` watches the explicit owner, while lines 47 and 80 recursively weigh its children. For example, changing only `first_vocation_vitals_postgres_tests.rs` changes the primary shard's starting weight without touching a watched input. A fresh and an incremental build of the same shard can then select different mounts. Register the out-of-directory files actually read by `source_bytes`. The existing directory watch does cover adding a new entry inside `postgres_tests/`.
